decisions.title: Substrate choice: Claude Code primitives vs. orchestration-framework alternative
decisions.context: The pipeline must run somewhere. The corpus explicitly names three out-of-scope alternatives (LangGraph, Temporal, AWS Step Functions) and grounds the design entirely in Claude Code primitives. This decision sets the boundary for every downstream design choice.
risks: Loss of declared cycles (mitigated by orchestrator-side counters per C-0013)
Loss of deterministic replay (acknowledged out-of-scope in C-0003)
Dependence on tenant-specific primitives (e.g., Task tool, AskUserQuestion)

decisions.title: Memory architecture: two-tier (orchestrator + per-sub-agent) vs. single-tier MEMORY.md
decisions.context: Sub-agents run in isolated contexts and have no native auto-loaded memory file (C-0021 — flagged 🔶 engineering proposal in source). The pipeline either accepts no per-agent persistence (single tier) or layers a convention on top of the file system (two tier). The two-tier proposal is the source's most consequential single-sourced claim — it has no precedent.
risks: Engineering proposal — no substrate-validated precedent (C-0021 flagged 🔶)
Single-sourced claim — RICE confidence calibrated to 0.5 (vendor-only provenance equivalent)
Sub-agent memory files may accumulate stale entries without periodic pruning discipline (C-0024 mitigates with 'do not pre-populate' rule)

decisions.title: Verification regime: vertical-slice early verification gate vs. end-to-end-only acceptance
decisions.context: Both source documents converge on the early-verification-point discipline (cross-source bridge at E-0012). The technical-designer source defines it abstractly; the synthesis-pipeline-technical-design source applies it concretely as the §7.4 vertical-slice gate (the very work this run replicates). This is the strongest cross-source signal in the corpus.
options_summary: Vertical-slice early gate (recommended by both sources)
risks: If the gate passes but the substrate later fails, the gate gave false confidence
Gate failure forces design re-revision — high cost, but catches substrate mismatch early
Output comparison method is the binding mechanism — without a captured reference, the gate is unverifiable on later runs (mitigation: capture reference artifacts per §7.4 criterion 6)

decisions.title: Recursion safety: hard rule (orchestrator + agent both check) vs. soft convention
decisions.context: The pipeline reads `output/**/*.md` and writes to `output/synthesis-<topic>/`. Without rigid exclusion, every re-run ingests its own prior output. The corpus states this is a hard rule (C-0019), enforced both at the orchestrator's input scan and at the sub-agent's secondary check (defense in depth).
options_summary: Hard rule with defense-in-depth (orchestrator + agent both check)
risks: If exclusion logic regresses, claim corpus pollutes itself silently
Defense-in-depth doubles verification cost (acceptable — both checks are cheap globs)

decisions.title: User confirmation: required AskUserQuestion gate vs. assumed defaults vs. configuration file
decisions.context: Three concurrent constraints (input set, target substrate, hard constraints) need confirmation before the pipeline runs. The corpus mandates an AskUserQuestion gate as a required interrupt with explicit cancellation handling (C-0008, C-0009). This shapes the pipeline's contract with the user.
risks: AskUserQuestion adds an interrupt to every run; users running scripted pipelines need a flag to bypass (out of scope for this design)
Cancellation handling must be explicit (C-0009 — empty answers exit cleanly without allocating run-id)
